rules.rule_context: FOIL requests received by the City are subject to the New York State Freedom of Information Law response timelines. A request is within scope of statutory processing from the date of departmental acknowledgement until either (a) responsive records are provided, (b) a formal denial with appeal rights is issued, or (c) a written extension notice is sent by the Records Access Officer citing good cause under Public Officers Law section 89. A request that has been acknowledged but not yet assigned to a processing unit remains an active FOIL matter; its queue position and pending status do not remove it from the statutory framework. Closing a request as unprocessable without a determination on the merits or a referral to the Records Access Officer for extension takes the matter outside the statutory process. The test for whether an action preserves statutory compliance is whether the original receipt date and acknowledgement remain operative, whether the requester receives either records or a legally sufficient reason for delay, and whether the City Records Access Officer is the only authority who may issue a time extension.
